content.p: On the afternoon of Sunday 14 December 2025, Rob Reiner, the actor and director behind "When Harry Met Sally...", "Stand By Me" and "This Is Spinal Tap", and his wife, the photographer and producer Michele Singer Reiner, were found dead in the master bedroom of their home in Brentwood, on the west side of Los Angeles. The Los Angeles County medical examiner gave the cause of death for both as multiple sharp force injuries. Their son Nick Reiner, who had been living on the property, was arrested the same night.

Nick Reiner has not been convicted of anything. He has pleaded not guilty, twice, to two counts of murder, and his case is in the pretrial stage. In September 2026 the Los Angeles County district attorney announced that prosecutors would not seek the death penalty, so the heaviest sentence he could face on conviction is life in prison without the possibility of parole. Prosecutors have not made a motive public.
content.h2: The day the couple were found
content.p: According to the Los Angeles Fire Department, the call for medical aid at the house on South Chadbourne Avenue came in at about 3:38 p.m., as the BBC reported. LAPD officers arrived at about 3:40 p.m., according to the police. Sources told CNN that the couple's daughter Romy, who lives across the street, checked on her parents at around 3 p.m., found their bodies, left the house and told a friend who was staying with her to call 911. Deadline reported that the couple were discovered by Romy and a friend, after a massage therapist due at the gated home could not get in. The wire report carried by the Jefferson City News Tribune said Romy went inside that afternoon, came upon her father's body and hurried out to a friend, who phoned 911.

The LAPD Assistant Chief, Dominic Choi, said the bodies were in the master bedroom. The district attorney's office said the couple had been fatally stabbed in the early morning hours of that Sunday. Death certificates, released by the county health department and reported by The Guardian, recorded the bodies as found at 15.45 and 15.46, the cause as "multiple sharp force injuries", the circumstances as "homicide" and the method as "with knife, by another". They list the interval between the onset of the attack and death as "minutes", and give the time and date of death as "unknown".

The medical examiner's findings on the causes of death were released on 17 December. The couple's ages were first reported variously: Michele Singer Reiner was initially given as 68 and then corrected to 70 on the medical examiner's figures, which CBS News used in its updated report. Rob Reiner was 78.

LAPD announced on Monday 15 December that Nick Reiner had been arrested and booked for murder. Police did not say what led them to him, saying only that the investigation had shown he was allegedly responsible. They located him at about 9:15 p.m. on the Sunday. The Associated Press placed the arrest in the Exposition Park area, close to USC, and said he did not resist; NBC News described the neighbourhood as University Park. Outlets also differ on the distance from the family home, with the Associated Press saying about 14 miles and NBC News about 15.

NBC Los Angeles obtained security camera video of the moment, which NBC News described: four police vehicles confronted a man in a black and green sweater, a hat and a red backpack as he crossed a street near Exposition Boulevard and Vermont Avenue, and he put his hands above his head. Moments earlier the video showed him in a gas station convenience store, waiting in line with a bottled drink. A clerk, Alexis Hernandez, said he looked like a typical customer. CBS News reported that Reiner had checked into a hotel in Santa Monica early that Sunday morning, about four miles from his parents' home; the movements after the killings were still under investigation at that point.

Reports of the interval between the discovery and the arrest vary. Fox 10 and FOX 13 put it at less than six hours after the bodies were found, while the Jefferson City News Tribune's version of a wire report said the arrest came roughly 12 hours after the couple were found stabbed to death.

Much of what has been said publicly about the evening before the killings comes from unnamed sources. Two people who attended a Saturday-night party at comedian Conan O'Brien's home told CBS News that Rob and Nick Reiner had a brief but loud argument there. Two people familiar with the situation told NBC News that Nick Reiner was disruptive at the event, and another source said he had interrupted a conversation involving the comedian Bill Hader and stormed off after being told it was private. Sources told ABC News, as reported by Good Morning America, that he was seen acting strangely. None of these accounts has been tested in court, and prosecutors have not said whether the argument has any bearing on the charges.

On Tuesday 16 December, District Attorney Nathan Hochman announced two counts of first-degree murder. He said the case qualified as special-circumstance murder because there were multiple victims, and the charges included an allegation that Reiner personally used a knife. Hochman said a conviction could mean life without parole or death and that his office had not decided which to pursue; he also said the family's views would be taken into consideration. He added that Reiner's mental health could come up in court if there was evidence of it, in whatever detail the defence chose to present it. Police chief Jim McDonnell said that charges were not evidence.

Reiner's first court appearance was on Wednesday 17 December. According to the Associated Press, he appeared from behind glass in a custody area, in shackles and a padded suicide-prevention smock, and said only "yes, your honor" to agree to postponing his arraignment until 7 January. He was held without bail. His lawyer, Alan Jackson, said the arraignment had earlier been held up because Reiner had not been medically cleared in time, and said the case involved "very, very complex and serious issues".
content.h2: A change of lawyers and the first plea
content.p: On 7 January 2026, Jackson, a prominent defence lawyer who had represented Harvey Weinstein in Los Angeles and Karen Read in Massachusetts, withdrew during the hearing. He told reporters the reasons were "circumstances beyond our control, but more importantly, circumstances beyond Nick's control." He also said: "Pursuant to the law in California, Nick Reiner is not guilty of murder." Hochman said he was confident that a jury would convict Reiner unanimously. The arraignment was put back to 23 February while a public defender, Kimberly Greene, took over.

On 23 February Greene entered not-guilty pleas to both counts. Deadline described a hearing of less than ten minutes in which bail was again refused. Reiner agreed to 29 April as the next date. Hochman told reporters that the defence would probably need extra time because of the volume of evidence, because prosecutors were still waiting for the coroner's report, and because any extra expert testimony would take time. A later NBC News report said Reiner had waived his right to a speedy trial.

On 29 April the case was put back again, after Greene told Judge Sam Ohta that the defence was still waiting for more evidence from prosecutors. Deputy District Attorney Habib Balian said the full autopsy report was still outstanding. Ohta set 15 September as the next date.
content.h2: What has been said about Reiner's health
content.p: Reiner's history of addiction was public long before the killings. In 2015 he co-wrote the film "Being Charlie" with his father directing; Rob Reiner called it "loosely based on things Nick went through and his relationship to me and his mother". Nick Reiner told People magazine in 2016 that he had spent weeks sleeping on the streets and had been in and out of rehabilitation programmes since he was 15. In an NPR interview in September 2025, Rob Reiner said his son had been "great" and had not used drugs for over six years, according to CNN.

After the killings, other details emerged through sources and records. FOX 13, citing records, said his mental health struggles included a schizophrenia diagnosis and a one-year conservatorship that lapsed in 2021; Deadline put the court-approved conservatorship at 2020 to 2021. Three sources with direct knowledge told NBC News that he received a schizophrenia diagnosis several years ago and that at some point before the killings his medication had been changed or adjusted. Deseret News reported, citing ABC News, that friends had told investigators his mental health had declined in the period before the deaths. Legal analysts quoted by KAXE and the Los Angeles Times said an insanity defence was a possibility and a difficult one, but the defence has not announced its strategy. After the death penalty decision, Greene said in a statement: "Nick has a serious mental illness and a long history of struggling with self-medication."

On 12 August, prosecutors unsealed an indictment that a grand jury had returned on 20 July. It replaced the original complaint and kept the two murder counts, with special-circumstance allegations of multiple murders and, newly, murder by means of lying in wait. The special allegation that he personally used a knife was also in the indictment. The district attorney's office said Reiner pleaded not guilty to the indictment that day.

The indictment spares witnesses a public preliminary hearing. TheWrap and the Jefferson City News Tribune said it lets prosecutors avoid a preliminary hearing and could move the case toward trial more quickly. Hochman said in a statement: "This was a profound betrayal by someone who was loved and trusted by the very people he is accused of killing." A lawyer quoted by Vulture, Neama Rahmani, said that the lying-in-wait allegation suggested prosecutors want to show premeditation, and that witnesses from the party might be important. That is one lawyer's reading, not something prosecutors have said.

The lying-in-wait allegation also meant the death penalty was possible. FOX 10 reported that the indictment noted aggravating factors involving high cruelty and particularly vulnerable victims. Reiner's older brother Jake has testified before the grand jury, according to ABC7.
content.h2: No death penalty, and what is still open
content.p: On 15 September, before the pretrial hearing, Hochman announced at a news conference that his office would not seek the death penalty. He said the decision followed a review of aggravating and mitigating factors, talks with the victims' families, and consultations with law enforcement and prosecutors. The Associated Press noted that California has not carried out an execution in two decades and that Gov. Gavin Newsom imposed a moratorium in 2019. If convicted, Reiner, who turned 33 in September, now faces at most life without parole.

At the hearing Reiner agreed to a general time waiver, which FOX 10 said effectively puts the trial off until at least 2027; Hochman told reporters he did not expect a trial this year. Several matters are still open:

Grand jury transcripts. Judge Ohta conditionally sealed the grand jury transcripts and exhibits and gave media organisations until late September to challenge that, with a hearing set for 7 October. Hochman's office did not oppose releasing them. Jake and Romy Reiner opposed it, with prosecutors' filings quoting them as saying disclosure "will cause them additional trauma and harm". The defence asked for permanent sealing to protect Reiner's right to a fair trial. How the 7 October hearing turned out has not been reported.

Trust fund. In June, Reiner's civil lawyers petitioned for the release of at least $1.5 million from a trust his parents set up for him, saying it was due to be paid out when he turned 30 and was needed for his defence. The trustees argue he should not receive it, while his lawyers say he is legally innocent and the money would be his regardless. A different judge is hearing this; a probate hearing was set for 23 October. Reiner wants the money to rehire Jackson, who has said he wants to return to the case.

The couple's other two children, Jake and Romy, have asked for privacy. Their first statement, on 17 December, said: "They weren't just our parents; they were our best friends." In August 2026 Jake Reiner gave his first sit-down interview, to ABC7 in Los Angeles, and said the months since had been a "living nightmare". He said he has not spoken with his brother, and has not attended the court hearings. Rob Reiner, who was married to Michele for 36 years, received a posthumous Emmy in September 2026 for a guest role in "The Bear", the night before the death penalty announcement. Nick Reiner remains in custody without bail.
